clue.text: Try hat, scratching head with charm

indicators.note: to scratch out the head of the word hat is to strike off its first letter

parts.note: to charm or lure someone is to tempt them

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to woo a person by doffing a hat and turning on the charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' removes the H of HAT, leaving AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Try and attempt are synonyms as verbs: to make an effort at something.

clue.text: Pretend European court supports a couple of fines

indicators.note: supports in a down clue means sitting underneath, so these pieces come after

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, so two of them are FF

explanation.surface: A European court props up a pair of penalties, pretending to be fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect an air or accent is to feign or put it on.

clue.text: Removing feet from trap, US man gets injury

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot of each word is its last letter, so each of the three words loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An American freed from a snare has been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAP, US and MAN each lose their end letter, giving TRA, U and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is physical injury or emotional shock, so injury is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Turkey is part of this set meal I'd ordered around beginning of December

indicators.note: around means wrapping, so the other piece goes inside
ordered means arranged, so the letters of set meal I'd are put in a new order
beginning of means only the first letter of December

explanation.surface: A December set menu with turkey is the Christmas dinner on order.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey looks like the Christmas bird; it is the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The country Turkey, straddling Europe and Asia, is counted in the region of south-west Asia.

clue.text: Belief that goes up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading the same going up and down means the word is the same read either way

parts.note: the definition word itself is the palindrome; the setter uses it once as definition and once as the word that reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: A conviction that fluctuates.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held to be true.

clue.text: Weapon wounded large animal

parts.note: wounded with a blade means cut
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an ass is a donkey, an animal

explanation.surface: A weapon has injured a big beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, the classic pirate's weapon.

clue.text: These go with shirts — clobber on golf course

parts.note: to clobber someone is to hit them, or cuff them
links is a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: Garments to wear with shirts and kit for the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobber' is British slang for clothing, which fits the surface, but here it is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cufflinks fasten the cuffs of dress shirts, so they are worn with them.

clue.text: Some golden retriever picked up bird

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, so the letters read upwards
some means only part of the words golden retriever is taken

explanation.surface: Part of a dog's job: a golden retriever fetches a shot bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' finds NRET in goldeN RETriever; 'picked up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tern is a slender seabird with forked tail, related to gulls.

clue.text: A note ignored by sentimentalist is sweet-smelling

indicators.note: ignored by means left out of the following word

parts.note: a sentimentalist is a romantic

explanation.surface: A soppy person overlooks a written message about something fragrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' means N, not a musical letter: ROMANTIC loses N to give ROMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means having a pleasant, spicy fragrance.

clue.text: Nose is broken in ship's drinking bouts

indicators.note: in means placed within the other piece

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters of nose is are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's nose gets broken in a brawl aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns NOSE IS into ESSION, which goes inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is informal British for a long spell of drinking, so bouts of it fit.

clue.text: Deception from German woman with diamonds

parts.note: Frau is German for woman or wife
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A German lady with jewels is suspected of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud is criminal deception, tricking someone for gain.

clue.text: Almost imprisoning female with debts? Extremely wicked

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: almost means near, as in near enough
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts give IOUS

explanation.surface: A woman nearly jailed over money she owes seems a very bad lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious describes villainy of a flagrant kind, so very wicked is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Utterly empty cell, criminal has nothing inside

indicators.note: has, together with inside, says the shell holds the other piece within it
inside, with has, places the letter for nothing within the rearranged letters
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of empty cell are bent out of shape

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A jail cell stands bare: the offender has nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges EMPTY CELL to CMPLETELY, and 'has nothing inside' puts O within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly and completely both mean totally, in every respect.

clue.text: Drink shark oil regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: An instruction to swallow fish-liver oil routinely, like a tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki is a variant spelling of sake, the Japanese rice wine.

clue.text: Boss renegotiated overall sum

indicators.note: renegotiated means dealt with afresh, so the letters of overall sum are rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager has redone the deal on a total figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager; it is slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss is informal slang for excellent, and marvellous means wonderful.

clue.text: Splitting up, say, soldiers in depot

indicators.note: in signals that one group sits inside another word

parts.note: a depot can be a bus or rail station
say introduces an example, abbreviated EG
soldiers are men in the ranks

explanation.surface: Troops at a base are being divided up.
explanation.definitionFit: Segmentation is division into separate parts, the process of splitting something.

clue.text: Significant second Oscar just unveiled?

parts.note: a second is a moment
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: unveiled means stripped of its cover, so the outer letters of just are removed

explanation.surface: A runner-up's Academy Award only just revealed, a big event.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentous means of great importance or consequence.

clue.text: Defendant maintaining Republican is loathsome

indicators.note: maintaining means holding or keeping within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a defendant in court is the accused

explanation.surface: A defendant who sticks to his politics is hateful.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means detestable or hateful, as if under a curse.

clue.text: Country is upset about resistance by dull American

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the next letter goes inside
upset in a down clue means overturned, so the word is runs upwards

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
lank describes hair that is limp and lifeless, dull

explanation.surface: A nation gets upset over opposition from a boring US visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses IS to SI, which goes 'about' R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is the island nation off the southern tip of India.

clue.text: Cold hermit saves desperately for when stockings go up?

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild disorder, so the letters of hermit saves are scrambled

explanation.surface: A chilly recluse scrimps hard for some occasion involving hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Children hang stockings up for presents on the night before 25 December.

clue.text: Make old boy fib about leader of government

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the next letter goes inside

parts.note: a fib is a lie

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of government

explanation.surface: Forcing a former pupil to tell untruths about a government boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone to do something is to make or compel them.

clue.text: Lower debt — cut by 50% on average?

indicators.note: cut by fifty percent means keeping only half the letters of debt

parts.note: a mean is an average

explanation.surface: Reducing borrowing by half compared with the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like a verb about reducing debt; it is demean, to degrade.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean oneself is to lower one's dignity or standing.

clue.text: Bug likes eating fruit

indicators.note: eating means the words Bug likes hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: An insect is fond of feeding on fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo hybrid with a wrinkly skin.

clue.text: Foolproof plan if ill, be converting papa's shed

indicators.note: converting means changing form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
shed means cast off, so this letter is dropped from plan

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sick person's foolproof scheme involves a change of plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papa's shed' drops P from PLAN, leaving LAN to mix with IF, ILL and BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolproof means incapable of going wrong, which is what infallible says.

clue.text: What rug might go on first?

definitions.meaning: rug is slang for a toupee or wig, which sits on a head
first means in front or in the lead

explanation.walkthrough: 'rug' looks like a floor covering; it is slang for a hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the lead or in front of others is being first.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, is left ecstasy

parts.note: is is taken as written; the letters running across is left only coincidentally match, this is a charade not a hidden word
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man is said to have quit his drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, hence 'perhaps' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is an example of an island, as in the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Rock star's first and second sound

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the word star's is used

parts.note: a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: A rock star's debut and follow-up have their own sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock star' looks like a music phrase; Rock alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock made of compacted sand grains.

clue.text: Be east of old tree

indicators.note: east of in an across clue means placed to the right, after the other piece

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay to the east of an ancient tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a Mediterranean evergreen grown for its fruit and oil.

clue.text: Prize returned by small boxers?

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a prize is a reward
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A trophy given back by little fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxers' suggests fighters, but it is the underwear; the question mark flags that it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are an example of underpants, which are old-fashionedly called drawers.

clue.text: Ring new rep about leaving parking spot

parts.note: a disc is a round flat ring-like shape

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so this letter is taken out
about means turned round, so the word rep is read backwards

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A sales representative turns away from a car-park space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses REP to PER and 'leaving parking' removes P, leaving ER between DISC and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice it, and discern means to perceive or make out.
